html:
The Irish Civil War of 1922 to 1923 was fought between supporters and opponents of the Anglo-Irish Treaty that had created the Irish Free State.

It began when Free State forces, using guns lent by Britain, shelled anti-Treaty fighters out of the Four Courts in Dublin. The Free State army soon took the towns, and the war became a bitter guerrilla struggle. Michael Collins was killed in an ambush in County Cork in August 1922. The government executed 81 prisoners.

The anti-Treaty side called off its fight in May 1923. About 1,500 people died, fewer than in many civil wars, but the bitterness lasted generations. The two main parties of Ireland, Fine Gael and Fianna Fáil, grew from the two sides, the second founded by Éamon de Valera.
sum: The Irish Civil War of 1922 to 1923 was fought between supporters and opponents of the Anglo-Irish Treaty that had created the Irish Free State.
